reference: John of Damascus, De haeresibus c. 101, Migne PG 94 col. 765 (PDF p. 475 for the continuation): the 'Zayd' narrative, Mamed's wife, and the adultery claim
gist_en: Muhammad is said to have asked his companion Zayd to divorce his beautiful wife so Muhammad could take her, then making a law permitting remarriage; John calls this adultery.
why_excluded: Personal attack on named individuals (Muhammad and Zayd) rather than a doctrinal point; it accuses Muhammad of adultery. The legal consequences are doctrinal, so the polygamy passage (jd-07) carries that content. Orchestrator may reconsider.

reference: Bede, In Canticum Canticorum (PL 91, Cedar passage; column read as ~1089 from page header, not confirmed on the image)
gist_en: Bede glosses Cedar, Ishmael's son, and says the Saracens who descended from him are today hated by all peoples, a prophecy the nation confirms.
why_excluded: A generalising characterisation of a whole people (Saracens as hated by all) rather than a doctrinal or historical point about Islam; borderline, so listed for the orchestrator rather than selected.
